_comment: STRESS FIXTURE — not a real business model. Run with: npm run check:definitions
Every way a replaced definitions file has been seen to differ from the one the app
was authored against, in one payload:
acquisition   8 lifecycle steps against a 7-value reach profile (resampled), and
5 segment values against 3 figures (resampled). Renamed dimension:
'segment' where the fixtures ask for 'ICP/segment' first.
retention     funnel: null where a lifecycle used to be.
partnerships  a workflow the recipe catalog has never heard of. Its definitions
load, but nothing can route to it — eligibility comes from
WORKFLOWS in recipes.ts, and that is where it would have to be
added. Reported as a warning, not dropped.
broken        no goal.metric, and dimensions is a string. Dropped with an error.
alsobroken    not an object at all. Dropped with an error.
(absent)      P&L, Revenue engine, Cost & Burn, Activation, Expansion and
Monetisation are all gone. Every one of them is still routable, so
each must fall back to the carried table in semanticModel.ts and
still render — that fallback is the main thing this fixture proves.
EXPECTED RESULT: 2 parse errors (the two dropped entries) and 1 warning
(partnerships), with every catalog workflow still yielding usable semantics. The
check INVERTS on the errors: zero errors is a FAILURE, because it would mean the
normaliser stopped noticing. If this file ever throws instead of reporting, the
tolerance in data/ has regressed.
